about: Framework-agnostic adapter conformance spec (plan section 1.12). Every adapter implements each case as a fixture in its framework and must classify it as stated. 'evidence' names the layer the adapter produces: source (ast-grep patterns), static-cases (the static test-case collector, checked as if every test function were new), run-report (guarded run plus normalised JUnit report) or collection (collect-only IDs per tier). 'expect' is finding (the rule reports it), clean (the rule does not), or a normalised record or collected IDs the adapter must produce.

cases.situation: a test patches a function of an owned package by its dotted name
a test patches an attribute of an imported owned module object
a test rebinds an attribute of an owned module by assignment
a test builds a mock specced on an owned class
a test fakes only standard-library and third-party boundaries
a test carries a static skip marker with no recorded exception
the same static skip is covered by an ADR-backed house-style exception for its path
a test is marked for automatic reruns until green
a test is marked as an expected failure
a property test neither fixes nor reports its seed
a property test fixes its seed
owned production code branches on a test-marker environment variable
owned production code declares a parameter that exists only for tests
owned production code reads only real configuration
a fast-tier test opens a network connection
a fast-tier test starts a process
a fast-tier fixture starts a process during teardown
a fast-tier test catches the guard's error and carries on
a fast-tier test computes in memory and writes only its temporary directory; the report shows the tier's guards
a test writes a file under the user's real home directory
a test writes under its temporary directory and the redirected home
a test skips at runtime; the normalised record keeps the outcome and reason for the shared report check
an expected failure is normalised as xfail with its reason
each test function carries an inline behaviour comment, above it or in its body; one comment covers all parameter rows
a test function has comments but no behaviour comment
a test function's behaviour comment holds only placeholder text
a tier selector collects no tests
a tier selector lists exactly the tests it selects
